title: ID0458724-DC/Si-D/IL-[MP / P9 170000901] Replacement of Phoenix Contact

additional_info.subject: Inquiry Regarding Replacement of PhoenixContact EV-T2HPCC-DC 500A Liquid-Cooled Cable with Air-Cooled 250A (400A Boost) Cable
additional_info.body:
Dear Support Team,
I would like to clarify whether it is technically possible to replace the existing Phoenix Contact EV-T2HPCC-DC 500A liquid-cooled charging cable with a standard air-cooled 250A cable (with 400A boost capability).
Could you please advise:
Whether such a replacement is supported for our DC charger configuration.
What hardware or firmware adjustments (if any) would be required.
If there are any limitations or considerations (e.g., derating, certification, safety, or compatibility with the cooling control system) that should be considered prior to implementation.
Your guidance on the feasibility and required steps for this modification would be highly appreciated.
Serial Number: 170000901
Best regards,
Orel Lachiani

If this modification is a request you wish to pursue, it would need to be treated as a customized service. For such a service, a Purchase Order (PO) would be essential to cover the associated costs for evaluating feasibility, necessary hardware and software adjustments.
To move forward, I would like to ask if we should prepare a detailed official proposal for this Purchase Order. This proposal would include a more in-depth analysis of the requirements, potential limitations (such as derating), and estimated costs.

additional_info.subject: RE: 0458724 - ID0458724-DC/Si-D/IL-[MP / P9 170000901] Replacement of Phoenix Contact CRM:00472000446
additional_info.body:
Dear Orel,
Thank you for your prompt feedback regarding our quotation for replacing the liquid-cooled CCS cable with an air-cooled standard cable on your charging stations. I understand your initial assessment that this might appear to be a straightforward cable and software update. While your understanding regarding the minor wiring changes and updating the cable type through the SCB is correct, I'd like to provide a bit more insight into the full scope of work involved, which contributes to the overall cost.
The process is more comprehensive than a simple cable swap and involves several critical steps to ensure a safe, reliable, and properly documented conversion:
Detailed Component Assessment:
Before any physical work begins, we need to conduct a thorough assessment to identify all components that are part of the liquid-cooled system and how they interface with the charging station. This includes identifying all related sensors, control units, and power connections that need to be either removed, reconfigured, or bypassed.
Comprehensive Cable Management Plan:
It's not just about removing the cooled cable and installing a new one. We must meticulously identify and map out
all
existing cables to be removed and
all
new cables to be connected, ensuring proper routing, termination, and adherence to safety standards.
Liquid Cooling System Decommissioning:
This is a crucial and specialized step. We need to carefully plan and execute the removal of the cooling pump and, importantly, the proper and safe elimination/disposal of the cooling liquid. This requires specific procedures and environmental considerations, which differ significantly from working with air-cooled systems.
Documentation and Quality Assurance:
As this is a conversion from a specialized liquid-cooled system to a standard air-cooled one, and not a routine replacement, we are committed to providing comprehensive documentation. This includes:
Developing a detailed work instruction:
This ensures every step is performed correctly and consistently.
Creating safety protocols:
Specifically for the decommissioning of the liquid system.
This documentation is essential for maintaining the long-term integrity and serviceability of your charging stations, and it requires significant engineering and technical time, as it falls outside of our standard, routine activities.
The quotation reflects the specialized nature of these tasks, the engineering effort required for planning and documentation, and the expertise needed to safely manage the transition from a liquid-cooled to an air-cooled system. Please note that this quotation represents an estimated time and cost for the activity. Our final invoicing will be based on the actual number of hours taken to complete the work, ensuring you only pay for the effort truly expended.
With best regards,
Joao Francisco Louro Cardoso

additional_info.subject: RE: 0458724 - ID0458724-DC/Si-D/IL-[MP / P9 170000901] Replacement of Phoenix Contact CRM:00472000446
additional_info.body:
Hi Joao,
Thank you very much for your detailed response — I truly appreciate the comprehensive explanation, and I fully understand the scope and complexity involved in the conversion process.
We are interested in moving forward and approving your offer so the process can begin. However, the current pricing model based on actual working hours is challenging for us when presenting this internally and especially when pricing the work for the end customer. Our customers expect a fixed and transparent total cost, and an open-ended cost structure makes it difficult for us to provide a clear quotation on our side.
A fixed and final price from your side would enable us not only to proceed with approving the offer, but also to accurately price our own portion of the work in the proposal to the end customer.
Thank you again for your support and cooperation.
Best regards,
Orel
